rows.why: The hosting environment's dependencies and connections to external networks and the internet (serving endpoints, registries, providers) are documented.
The costs of a hosting compromise, outage or cost abuse (stolen compute, runaway spend, downtime) are examined and tied to risk tolerance.
The servers, GPUs, registries, serving software and third-party hosting material the org relies on are inventoried and their risks mapped.
Third-party hosting material (base images, serving software, models and packages pulled from registries, provider services) is reviewed for security vulnerabilities and approved before it is used.
The likelihood and magnitude of hosting compromise, outage and cost abuse are assessed, drawing on past incidents and provider reports, to prioritise treatment.
Hosts and serving endpoints are monitored in production for anomalies such as unusual load, cost spikes, configuration changes or tampering.
The hosted service is tested to fail safely and recover under high load, resource exhaustion and component failure.
Security and resilience of the hosting environment and exposed endpoints are tested through vulnerability scans and adversarial exercises.
Administrative, registry, secret-access and endpoint activity on the hosting environment is logged so actions can be traced and accounted for.
Controls that sustain the hosted service (authenticated access, network isolation, throttling, firewalling) are in place and applied.
Procedures exist and are followed to respond to and recover hosting from compromise, outage or abuse, including restoring from backups.
The org can rapidly disable or isolate a hosted endpoint or revoke its keys when compromise or cost abuse is detected.
Risks from third-party infrastructure used for hosting (cloud, GPU and registry providers) are monitored and controls applied.
Post-deployment plans for the hosting environment cover patching and change management, backups and recovery.
Hosting incidents and errors are tracked, communicated, reviewed after the fact and documented.

review.reason: Why leaves out secrets, keys and the model registry, which the area covers, and cis_refs omit LLM-4.6 (centralised, scoped secret management) and LLM-4.1 (hardened serving configuration), which support it.
Backups and recovery repeat the restore-from-backup check in MANAGE 2.3 (and LLM-11.x refs); keep this row to patching and change management of the hosting stack, or drop the overlap.
Outage and cost abuse harm the processes that depend on the hosted model, not only assets; the area's impacts may be too narrow.
Failing safely under load or component failure protects the processes relying on the service; the area's impacts (assets only) may be too narrow.
